SMTO-HTTP-0022 — The request points to a website outside the saved connection

GUID: 55d9bb63-5699-44ad-8616-42c99bf2133e
Slug: http-profile-origin-mismatch
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • A saved connection only allows its own website address and any extra addresses approved in its settings. SMTO tried to send a request or sign in somewhere else, so it was blocked and nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select the connection, and check that Base URL is the service's correct address, including https and any port number. Requests are only allowed to the website in Base URL, so a wrong address blocks them.
  2. If the service really uses a second address, such as a separate sign-in site, add it as an Allowed origin under Advanced connection settings, then select Save. An approved extra address lets sign-in or requests go there; only add addresses you trust, because sign-in details may be sent to them.
  3. Select Test connection, then ask SMTO in the conversation to repeat the request. The test confirms the corrected addresses work before SMTO tries again.

What success looks like

  • Test connection succeeds and SMTO's request shows the service's reply.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't add unfamiliar addresses just to get past this; the check stops your sign-in details from reaching the wrong website.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A resource or authentication URL resolved to an origin that is neither the HTTP profile's base origin nor one of its explicitly allowed origins.

What this means

  • The authentication or resource URL resolves outside the profile's bound/explicitly allowed origins. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The authentication or resource URL resolves outside the profile's bound/explicitly allowed origins.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare resolved scheme, host and port with the profile's base and explicit allowed origins, including authentication endpoints.

How to fix it

  • prepare_request (gateway_core/http_contract.py) and AuthFlow.endpoint (gateway_core/http_auth/flow.py) reject a resource or authentication URL whose origin is not origin(base_url) or in allowed_origins; normalize_profile applies the same check to auth endpoints when the profile is saved. Correct base_url, the token/authorization/device endpoints or issuer, or add the intended origin to allowed_origins; never disable origin enforcement.
  • Correct the base and authentication origins in the selected profile without bypassing origin protection.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended explicit request uses an approved origin and redirects retain their separate protections.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
